## Result: Skewness of Gene Expression Distribution

**Skewness (Fisher, `scipy.stats.skew`, bias=True): 0.6897**

| Statistic | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Skewness | **0.689708** |
| Mean | 2.611995 |
| Median | 2.342318 |
| Std | 2.504827 |
| Min | −2.623208 |
| Max | 18.436851 |
| N (pooled) | 32,017,874 (1,673 cell lines × 19,138 genes) |

**Qualitative description:** The pooled log₂(TPM+1) gene expression distribution is **moderately right-skewed (positive skew, γ₁ ≈ 0.69)**. The mean (2.61) exceeds the median (2.34), consistent with a right tail of highly expressed genes pulling the mean upward. This is the expected shape for log-transformed count/TPM data: most genes are expressed at moderate-to-low levels (bulk near 0–3), while a subset of highly expressed genes extends the right tail.

### Method
- Pooled all 32,017,874 expression values (all 1,673 cell lines × all 19,138 protein-coding genes) into a single 1-D array.
- Computed Fisher's skewness via `scipy.stats.skew(pooled)` with default `bias=True`.
- No re-transformation (values already log₂(TPM+1), batch-corrected).
- No cell-line filtering; all rows in the expression file used.
